news.title: Dating apps must carry an 18+ rating on the App Store
news.body: From 16 November, developers must say whether their apps include dating or relationship features, including virtual companions with romantic content, and whether they share real-world location. Dating apps will need a minimum 18+ rating (A18 in Brazil). Everyone has until 12 January 2027 to submit both answers in App Store Connect.

news.title: Supreme Court will hear Apple’s Epic appeal on 11 January
news.body: Oral arguments are set for 11 January 2027. Apple is appealing the 2025 contempt ruling that said it broke the original injunction by limiting external payment links and charging commission on outside purchases. The court is reviewing only the contempt finding; what Apple may charge is being handled separately by the district court.

news.title: Apple sends spyware warnings to users in 99 countries
news.body: Apple sent a new round of threat notifications saying some people may have been targeted by mercenary spyware. The Financial Times, as relayed by 9to5Mac, says German officials were among those warned and that the attacks reportedly used a zero-click flaw. Apple does not name who is behind it and recommends Lockdown Mode for recipients.

news.title: iOS 27.2.1 in testing; iOS 27.3 beta due this week
news.body: MacRumors saw iOS 27.2.1 in its visitor logs, likely a small fix update that includes iPhone Duo. Apple’s China newsroom said the iOS 27.3 beta arrives 4 November (likely 3 November in the US), with a public release in December. It turns on some Apple Intelligence features in China, using Alibaba’s Qwen for Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence.

news.title: Apple posts a record September quarter: $114.5 billion
news.body: Revenue rose 12% to $114.5 billion and earnings per share were $2.10, up 14%. Apple reports record iPhone revenue for the quarter, an all-time high for Services and a record $479 billion for the fiscal year. Tariff refunds added about $0.05 to earnings per share.

news.title: Ternus: no end date for iPhone Duo shortages
news.body: Speaking after the earnings report, CEO John Ternus said Apple is supply-constrained on iPhone Duo and can’t predict when supply and demand will balance. Orders placed on earnings day show January delivery estimates. He added that only a very small share of units have been returned over the inner-display issue, and Apple is sending replacements.

news.title: New tvOS 27.2 build for the updated Apple TV 4K
news.body: Apple released tvOS 27.2 build 24K154 only for the new fourth-generation Apple TV 4K, which launches 13 November at $299. Existing models stay on build 24K122. Apple hasn’t published release notes; one report says the build turns on Siri AI for the new box.

news.title: Apple's first touchscreen Mac: the OLED MacBook Pro
news.body: The 14-inch ($2,899) and 16-inch ($3,399) MacBook Pro get a tandem-OLED “PROLED XDR” display with built-in touch, up to 2,000 nits and 10Hz–120Hz refresh. The notch gives way to a smaller Dynamic Island. Chips are M5 Pro or M5 Max, with up to 128GB of memory and 16TB of storage. Pre-orders opened 28 October; it arrives 6 November alongside the mini-LED models.

news.title: Apple first planned to launch iPhone Duo in November
news.body: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says Apple originally meant to wait until November and sell the Duo only in the US and China. It instead launched in more than 70 countries on 23 October, with too little stock for demand. Delivery estimates are around 25 January.

news.title: iPhone Duo buyer waits shrink to about 89 days
news.body: UBS Evidence Lab data as of 30 October puts the average Duo wait near 89 days, about a week shorter than the week before. UBS says the screen-crack reports are unlikely to be the main reason, and the data cannot show whether demand fell or supply improved.

news.title: Zoom and Microsoft Office apps now optimized for iPhone Duo
news.body: Zoom shows shared content and participants together on the inner display. Word, PowerPoint, Excel and OneNote have been updated, and Outlook has been optimized since launch. Teams is not yet. Apps built with the iOS 27.1 SDK or later fill both screens.

news.title: Display Zoom can’t be changed after Duo setup
news.body: The Default/Medium/Large text size is chosen during setup, but the usual Settings > Appearance > Display Zoom option is missing afterwards on iOS 27.2. One owner says Apple Support told them the only fix is to erase and set up again. Apple hasn’t commented.

news.title: A robotic HomeView with a 9-inch swiveling screen
news.body: The Information’s Aaron Tilley reports a prototype with a 9-inch display on a swiveling arm that uses cameras and sensors to act on its own, for around $1,000. Apple reportedly hopes for 2027, but it may slip to 2028. The name is unconfirmed.

news.title: HomeView may double as a security camera
news.body: Code sleuth pdfu found settings strings in HomeView software 27.2 describing HomeKit Secure Video camera modes (Off, Detect Activity, Stream, Stream & Allow Recording) with schedules. Apple hasn’t announced a camera feature, and it may not be there at launch on 13 November.

news.title: HomeView may mirror CarPlay apps like Spotify from an iPhone
news.body: A video from developer Steve Troughton-Smith shows Spotify running on a virtualized HomeView, apparently mirrored from a paired iPhone via CarPlay-style support. Apple hasn’t confirmed it.

news.title: The 14-inch MacBook Pro moves to M6
news.body: Apple announced the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 by press release: a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU, a dual 16-core Neural Engine, up to 170GB/s memory bandwidth, and Wi‑Fi 7 with Bluetooth 6. Apple says graphics are up to 30% faster than M5. It starts at $1,999 with 1TB, in Space Black and Silver. Pre-orders open October 28; it arrives November 6. The design is unchanged.
srcs: Apple Newsroom: 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6

news.title: iMac gets M6, Wi‑Fi 7 and faster Ethernet
news.body: The 24-inch iMac keeps its design and seven colours and moves to M6, with up to a 12-core CPU and GPU, a dual 16-core Neural Engine and up to 170GB/s memory bandwidth. Wi‑Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 come standard, and 12-core models get 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet and four Thunderbolt 4 ports. It costs $1,499 (10-core) or $1,699 (12-core). Pre-orders open October 28; it arrives November 6.

news.title: A future iPhone Duo may get a slightly bigger inner screen
news.body: Mark Gurman says Apple is weighing a Duo whose inner display is about half an inch larger than today’s 7.6 inches, roughly 7.9 to 8.1 inches. He says it would not be a separate Max model and the outer screen would grow little. Reports differ on which generation gets it. Not confirmed by Apple.

news.title: Apple teases an “exciting week” after the iPad mini
news.body: Marketing chief Greg Joswiak hinted at more launches right after the OLED iPad mini. M6 iMac and MacBook Pro updates and a touchscreen MacBook Pro are expected, with hands-on sessions in Los Angeles on Wednesday.
see: The Pro and Tell event page

news.title: Apple reportedly asks for 30% more iPhone Duo production
news.body: Taiwan’s Economic Daily reports that strong demand led Apple to ask suppliers for about 30% more units, lifting 2026 shipment estimates from about 6 million to 8–10 million. A second wave of shipments is expected from January 22.

news.title: Apple responds to iPhone Duo screen cracks
news.body: Apple says it is aware of an inner display issue on a small number of iPhone Duo units and asks affected owners to contact AppleCare for a replacement. It hasn’t said what causes it or how many phones are affected.

news.title: iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2 are out
news.body: Siri AI can now remember earlier conversations and draw on Messages photos, Calendar attendees, voicemails and Safari history, and it adds French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish (not in the EU or mainland China). Messages suggests actions, Apple TV gets profiles, and HomePod gets touch lock controls. The redesigned Health app was held back for later this year.
see: The release candidate, a week earlier

news.title: iPhone Duo gets Apple Pencil support
news.body: iOS 27.2 brings Apple Pencil to iPhone Duo’s inner display, earlier than Apple’s “later this year” promise. Only the USB-C Apple Pencil works; Apple Pencil Pro and older models aren’t supported.

news.title: watchOS, tvOS, visionOS, macOS and HomePod 27.2 arrive too
news.body: watchOS 27.2 brings the Siri AI memory and languages to Apple Watch and makes Siri respond faster. tvOS 27.2 adds HomePod surround sound, HomePod 27.2 brings Sound Glow to existing HomePods, and visionOS 27.2 is mostly fixes. macOS Golden Gate 27.2 shipped the same day.

news.title: Pre-orders sell out into January within hours
news.body: Apple called demand “nothing short of extraordinary” as delivery estimates for every color and storage size slipped to late January 2027.

news.title: Verizon apologizes for pre-order delays
news.body: The carrier offered affected iPhone Duo customers a $100 gift card.

news.title: In-store pickup returns in the US and Canada
news.body: After a launch with long lines and limited stock, Apple Store pickup went live again.

news.title: Shortcuts can run when you open or close the Duo
news.body: Personal automations can trigger on folding and unfolding the phone.

news.title: Apple’s foldable will be called iPhone Duo
news.body: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported Apple had settled on the name ahead of the September event.
news.statusNote: Apple announced iPhone Duo on 9 Sep 2026.

news.title: A second foldable iPhone in 2027
news.body: Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo said Apple planned a follow-up foldable for 2027, the iPhone’s 20th anniversary.

news.title: iPhone Duo 2 prototypes have Face ID under the outer display
news.body: Apple is reportedly testing under-display Face ID for a successor expected next fall, but hasn’t decided whether it will ship. Gurman had earlier expected it with the third model.

news.title: An Action button is under consideration
news.body: Apple is said to be weighing a physical Action button for a future Duo, and may keep or drop Touch ID in the power button. Nothing is final.

news.title: iPhone Duo 2 with three rear cameras
news.body: A leaker claims the next Duo adds a third camera and may drop the nano-texture display finish, possibly as soon as spring 2027.

news.title: Apple plans to fix Safari’s cramped layout
news.body: A report says Apple wants to improve how Safari uses the Duo’s displays in a software update.

news.title: 9to5Mac: “The future is foldable”
news.body: Chance Miller praises a hinge that feels fantastic, the compact footprint and the 7.6-inch inner display.

news.title: Engadget: “A first-class foldable”
news.body: Cherlynn Low says Apple sidestepped most first-generation growing pains, with strong marks for the display, battery, cameras and performance.

news.title: CNN: Apple’s coolest phone in years
news.body: Positive, with one big caveat: the roughly $2,000 price, about what a 14-inch MacBook Pro costs.

news.title: The Verge: expensive and full of compromises
news.body: Nilay Patel and Allison Johnson found it frustrating to use for the price.

news.title: PetaPixel: “A compromise, but not compromised”
news.body: A camera-focused review: the Duo gives up some photo hardware to fold, but the results hold up.

news.title: Tech Advisor: “Remarkable but not flawless”
news.body: Impressed overall, with reservations.

news.title: JerryRigEverything: fails the dust test
news.body: The Duo struggled in JerryRigEverything’s durability test with dust, despite its IP68 rating.

news.title: iFixit teardown: provisional 5 out of 10
news.body: The inner display and hinge are the hardest parts to repair, and iFixit found dust inside the hinge. For comparison, the Galaxy Z Fold8 and Pixel 11 Pro Fold each scored 4. Teardowns also found two batteries.

news.title: Inner screens cracking along the hinge
news.body: Some owners report a crack or a line of bright pixels along the fold, in one case after fewer than 20 openings. How widespread it is isn’t known. Teardowns point to possible hinge causes, but Apple hasn’t confirmed a defect.
news.statusNote: On 26 October Apple said it is aware of an issue affecting the inner display on a small number of units and asked owners to contact AppleCare for a replacement. It hasn’t given a cause.

news.title: Safari feels cramped on the Duo
news.body: Safari doesn’t make full use of the Duo’s displays yet.

news.title: Older apps appear letterboxed on the inner display
news.body: Apps built with the iOS 26 SDK or earlier sit in the middle of the inner display with empty space around them. Apps built with the iOS 27 SDK resize to fill most of it, and those built with iOS 27.1 use the full display.
news.statusNote: Fixed app by app as developers update.

news.title: Apple announces an OLED iPad mini
news.body: An 8.5-inch OLED display, the A20 Pro chip (the same chip as iPhone Duo), a 5.4 mm design with IP67 water resistance, from $699. Pre-orders open October 28; it arrives November 6.

news.title: The camera can show your subject a preview on the outer display
news.body: With iPhone Duo open, the outer display can mirror the camera frame so the person you’re photographing can see the shot before you take it.

news.title: A setting keeps case edges from covering the outer display
news.body: Shift Left Edge, in Display & Brightness settings, adds a border so content isn’t hidden behind a case.

news.title: An OLED iPad mini this month
news.body: Reports ahead of Pro and Tell said an OLED iPad mini could be part of Apple’s late-October launches.

news.body: The standard iPhone 18 and the 18e are expected in spring rather than September, both with the A20 chip.

news.title: iPhone Air 2 in the first half of 2027
news.body: A version of the A20 Pro, a second rear camera, a bigger battery and vapor-chamber cooling.

news.body: The budget MacBook would move up from the A18 Pro with 8GB, and add new colors, in the first half of 2027.

news.body: OLED MacBook Air and iMac models are still in testing, so the next versions are expected to keep LCD displays.

news.title: OLED iPad Air in the first half of 2027
news.body: The iPad Air would follow the iPad Pro and the new iPad mini to OLED.

news.title: No new Vision Pro for at least two years
news.body: Apple is researching a lighter, cheaper headset but nothing is in active development, and the “Vision Air” was reportedly canceled.

news.title: iPhone 18 Pro restarted when Face ID failed
news.body: iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max could restart unexpectedly after a failed Face ID attempt.

news.title: Touchscreen froze with both Centers open
news.body: On iOS 27, opening Notification Center and Control Center together could make the screen stop responding.

news.title: Command-line tools still trust compromised certificates
news.body: Apple has blocked compromised eMudhra certificates in Safari, Mail and apps since October 19, but command-line tools on the Mac can still accept them.
news.statusNote: Apple says a macOS update will fix it; no date yet.

news.title: Home Screen edit mode can freeze the screen
news.body: Rearranging widgets or switching pages while editing the Home Screen can freeze the touchscreen until you force-restart. It doesn’t happen in normal use.
news.statusNote: Still present in iOS 27.0.1. Not yet confirmed fixed in iOS 27.2.

news.title: AirPods Pro 3 static with noise cancellation on
news.body: Owners report static or crackling with Active Noise Cancellation on and nothing playing, and some report sync problems with video.
news.statusNote: Several firmware updates followed, including 8B40 in May 2026 which improved noise cancellation, but none was confirmed to fix the static.

news.title: An exploited image-processing flaw on older software
news.body: A CoreGraphics flaw let a malicious file run code. Apple says it may have been used in targeted attacks against devices running versions before iOS 27.
news.statusNote: Fixed in iOS 26.7.1, macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1. OS 27 versions aren’t affected.

news.title: Apple Watch sent SMS instead of iMessage
news.body: With a dual-SIM iPhone, Messages on the watch could fall back to SMS, and Workout audio alerts could fail when the iPhone wasn’t nearby.

news.title: Apple Home Collection: cameras, a lock and thermostats
news.body: Alongside HomeView, Apple introduced a line of smart home accessories made with LG and Schneider Electric: a video doorbell, three cameras, a deadbolt lock that unlocks as you approach, two thermostats and room sensors, from $39.95.
